newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Six injured after clash in Indonesia's Irian Jaya.
newsitem.headline: Six injured after clash in Indonesia's Irian Jaya.

text.p: Two people were arrested and six were hurt when Indonesian police fired rubber bullets to quell protesters who rampaged through a town during an election rally in Irian Jaya, the military and news reports said on Tuesday.

The official Antara news agency said 20 homes, offices and shops were damaged after about 5,000 people at a campaign rally by the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) rioted on Monday at the town of Abepura near Jayapura, capital of Irian Jaya province.
It said six people were injured when police fired rubber bullets to disperse the protesters.

"Two people have been arrested after the incident. We are still investigating the case and there could be more to be arrested. But everything is under control now," a military spokesman told Reuters by telephone from Jayapura, 2,200 miles (3,500 kms), east of Jakarta.

Antara said the violence was not linked to clashes on the country's main Java island in the run-up to the May 29 elections. It said the PDI campaigners were blocked from entering Jayapura after the Abepura rally and a pregnant woman fell down bleeding during a scuffle with police.
The crowd then became violent, it said.

Jakarta and other areas of Java were hit by clashes at the weekend between supporters of the other two parties in the election contest -- the ruling Golkar and the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP).

Remote Irian Jaya is home to the Free Papua Movement, which has waged a sporadic battle against Indonesian rule. Six foreigners and three Indonesians were rescued last May after being kidnapped and held captive by the rebels for about four months.
Golkar, the PPP and PDI are the only parties legally entitled to contest the general elections. Golkar is expected to win easily after taking 68 percent of the vote in the last elections in 1992.
